# Results — Study 133 (Crypto-Seasonality) on real BTC-USD daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly returns for BTC-USD
computed from Yahoo Finance daily closes, entry at each month's first-day open (no
look-ahead), exit at each month's last-day close. Each month's HAC t-stat is measured
vs the all-month mean return (the correct baseline when BTC has a secular trend).
Bonferroni-corrected for 12 simultaneous tests. As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| BTC-USD (Yahoo Finance, daily) | 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-14 | 142 | `3c26b7c8e544` |

*~12 observations per calendar month — the study's structural power ceiling.*

## Per-month statistics (vs all-month baseline)

The all-month mean log-return is **+3.5%/month** (annualised Sharpe **+0.62**, HAC
*t* = +1.80 — BTC's secular bull run). Each month's t-stat measures excess above this
baseline. Bonferroni-corrected threshold for 12 tests: **|t| ≥ 3.1** (alpha = 0.05/12).

| Month | n | Mean (%) | Median (%) | Std (%) | HAC *t* | Naive sig (|t|≥2) | Bonferroni sig (|t|≥3.1) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|:--:|
| Jan | 12 | −3.3 | −3.6 | 21.8 | −1.14 | — | — |
| Feb | 12 | +8.7 | +11.8 | 17.4 | +1.24 | — | — |
| Mar | 12 | −1.1 | −0.2 | 19.0 | −0.78 | — | — |
| Apr | 12 | +8.8 | +9.7 | 16.6 | +0.84 | — | — |
| May | 12 | +4.4 | +3.2 | 27.1 | +0.12 | — | — |
| Jun | 12 | −1.0 | −0.6 | 19.7 | −0.85 | — | — |
| Jul | 11 | +8.4 | +8.1 | 10.6 | **+2.02** | * | — |
| Aug | 11 | −1.9 | −7.9 | 19.3 | −1.26 | — | — |
| **Sep** | 12 | **−3.4** | −4.5 | 8.5 | **−2.59** | * | — |
| **Oct** | 12 | **+15.1** | +12.9 | 16.6 | **+2.99** | * | — |
| Nov | 12 | +4.1 | +7.6 | 26.8 | +0.12 | — | — |
| Dec | 12 | +5.3 | −3.2 | 19.2 | +0.44 | — | — |

**Naive significant (|t| ≥ 2): 3/12 — Jul, Sep, Oct.** Under H₀ with 12 tests at
alpha=0.05 we expect ~0.6 false discoveries. Finding 3 is modestly above chance but not
dramatically so.

**Bonferroni significant (|t| ≥ 3.1): 0/12.** No month survives the family-wise error
correction. October at *t* = +2.99 misses by 0.11.

### Key months in detail

**October ('Uptober'):** mean +15.1%, median +12.9%, std ±16.6%, n=12.
Year-by-year: −12.7% (2014), +33.1% (2015), +14.9% (2016), +49.0% (2017), −4.6% (2018),
+10.8% (2019), +27.7% (2020), +39.9% (2021), +5.5% (2022), +28.6% (2023),
+10.9% (2024), −3.9% (2025).
Two exceptional Octobers (2017: +49%, 2021: +40%) drive much of the average.

**September ('Rektember'):** mean −3.4%, median −4.5%, std ±8.5%, n=12.
Notably low volatility (8.5% std vs all-month avg ~19%) — the bear signal is consistent
but small; year-by-year: −16.9%, +2.5%, +5.9%, −7.7%, −6.0%, −13.9%, −7.7%, −7.0%,
−3.1%, +4.0%, +7.4%, +5.4%.

## Seasonal long/flat rule vs buy-and-hold

All-month buy-and-hold: Sharpe **+0.62**, mean **+3.5%/month**, t = +1.80.

| Rule | Long months | Sharpe | Differential HAC *t* vs B&H |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| Uptober-only | Oct | +0.68 | −1.29 |
| Jul + Oct | Jul, Oct | +0.72 | −1.15 |
| Best-5 in-sample | Oct, Apr, Feb, Jul, Nov | +1.00 | +0.07 |
| Sep-only (bad month) | Sep | −0.40 | −1.96 |

No seasonal rule produces a statistically significant outperformance of buy-and-hold.
The 'Best-5 in-sample' differential t = +0.07 is noise and reflects in-sample data
mining (5 months chosen after observing their returns).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The real tape shows October at HAC *t* = +2.99 and September at
  −2.59 — genuine-looking signals. But with n=12 per month and 12 hypotheses, the
  correct inference bar is |t| ≥ 3.1 (Bonferroni) and zero months clear it. No month survives the
  Bonferroni bar — the apparent seasonality is a multiple-testing artefact.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No seasonal long/flat rule reliably beats buy-and-hold.
  The Uptober-only strategy has a slightly higher Sharpe (+0.68 vs +0.62) but the
  differential t is −1.29 (noise). The best in-sample selection has zero out-of-sample
  credibility.
- **Multiple comparisons — key finding.** The calendar narrative is built on searching
  12 months and highlighting winners. Testing all 12 formally and correcting for multiple
  comparisons eliminates the apparent signal entirely. This is the study's main result.
